A.subject: Physics
A.text: What is the magnitude of velocity of the image in mirror (1) with respect to the velocity of image in the mirror (2) in the situation as shown in figure?
A.sol_text:
Solution:

From the diagram, Mirror 1 is at 45° to the vertical.

The object moves upward with velocity v.

For Mirror 2 (vertical mirror):
The image in Mirror 2 moves with the same speed as the object but in opposite direction (horizontally).
Velocity of image in mirror 2 = v (perpendicular to mirror, moving right)

For Mirror 1 (at 45°):
The velocity component perpendicular to Mirror 1 is: v cos(θ) where θ = 45°
The velocity component parallel to Mirror 1 is: v sin(θ)

Breaking down the object's velocity v (upward):
- Component perpendicular to Mirror 1: v cos(45°) = v/√(2)
- Component parallel to Mirror 1: v sin(45°) = v/√(2)

The image velocity perpendicular to Mirror 1 (away from mirror) = v cos(45°) = v/√(2)

In vector form:
- v_cosθ component (perpendicular to mirror, going left-upward along mirror normal)
- v_sinθ component (parallel to mirror, downward along mirror surface)

Resolving for image in Mirror 1:
The reflected velocity has components:
- Along mirror normal: v cos(45°) = v/√(2)
- Along mirror surface: v sin(45°) = v/√(2)

Resultant velocity of image in Mirror 1 relative to Mirror 2:
Relative velocity = √[(v_image1)² + (v_image2)²]

From the geometry and reflection laws:
v_image1 has magnitude: √(2)v (shown in solution diagram)
v_image2 has magnitude: v

Relative velocity magnitude = √(2)v

Answer: (2) √(2)v

A.text: A screw gauge with a pitch of 0.5 mm and a circular scale with 50 divisions is used to measure the thickness of a thin sheet of Aluminium. Before starting the measurement, it is found that when the two jaws of the screw gauge are brought in contact, the 45th division coincides with the main scale line and that the zero of the main scale is barely visible. What is the thickness of the sheet if the main scale reading is 0.5 mm and the 25th division coincides with the main scale line?

Reading = 0.5 + 25 × 0.01 + 0.05 = 0.80 mm

A.subject: Physics
A.text:
The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by
vec(E) = E₀ î cos(kz) cos(ωt)

The corresponding magnetic field vec(B) is then given by:
(1) vec(B) = (E₀/c) ĵ sin(kz) cos(ωt)
(2) vec(B) = (E₀/c) ĵ cos(kz) sin(ωt)
(3) vec(B) = (E₀/c) ĵ sin(kz) sin(ωt)
(4) vec(B) = (E₀/c) k̂ sin(kz) cos(ωt)
A.sol_text:
Answer: (3)

Solution:
E₀/B₀ = C
∴ B₀ = E₀/c

Given that vec(E) = E₀ cos(kz) cos(ωt) î
vec(E) = (E₀/2)[cos(kz−ωt) î−cos(kz+ωt) î]

Correspondingly
vec(B) = (B₀/2)[cos(kz−ωt) ĵ−cos(kz+ωt) ĵ]
vec(B) = (B₀/2) × 2sin kz sin ωt
vec(B) = (E₀/c sin kz sin ωt) ĵ

A.sol_text:
Solution:

For C-1:
(4) H
(3) CH₃
(2) CH₂CH₃

Atom priorities by atomic number: H < C
For the three carbons attached to C-1:

- C≡CH: C with triple bond (counts as 3 bonds to C)

(2) CH₂CH₃
(3) CH₃
(4) H

C-1 → (R)

For C-2:
(4) H
(2) NH₂
(1) C≡N
(3) HO

Atom priorities by atomic number:
For atoms directly attached: N (14), C (6), O (8), H (1)
- C≡N: N with priority 7
- NH₂: N with priority 7
Compare: C≡N has triple bond to N; NH₂ has single bond to N
C≡N has higher priority

Between NH₂ and HO:
- NH₂: N (7)
- HO: O (8)

Priority assignment:
(1) C≡N
(2) NH₂
(3) HO
(4) H

C-2 → (R)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Major product A will be
options: OH with Me groups and CH₂—CH=¹⁴CH₂ attached to benzene ring
OH with Me groups and CH₂—CH=¹⁴CH₂ attached to benzene ring (different position)
OH with Me groups and ¹⁴CH₂—CH=CH₂ attached to benzene ring
OH with Me groups and ¹⁴CH₂—CH=CH₂ attached to benzene ring (different position)
A.sol_text:
Starting material: 2,6-dimethylphenyl allyl ether (O-CH₂-CH=CH₂ with two Me groups and ¹⁴C label on terminal carbon)

Under heat (Δ), this undergoes Claisen rearrangement:

The allyl ether rearranges to form a C-C bond to the benzene ring while the O-C bond breaks.

First intermediate: A dienone intermediate is formed with a C=O double bond at position 1 (ortho to the allyl side chain) and CH₂-CH=CH₂ as the allyl group, with CH₃ formed as a leaving group.

This dienone then undergoes further rearrangement under heat to form the final product.

Second heating step: The dienone converts to a phenol with OH group, where the allyl group migrates to the para position relative to one of the original methyl groups.

Final product (option 1): 2,6-dimethyl-4-allylphenol where the allyl chain CH₂-CH=¹⁴CH₂ is attached at the 4-position (para to the OH which is at position 1), with methyl groups at positions 2 and 6.

A.subject: Chemistry

(Q) → (4)

(i) KMnO₄, KOH, Δ
(ii) SOCl₂

This converts the methyl group to a carboxylic acid chloride (CO-Cl), which upon reduction with H₂/Pd-BaSO₄ gives Benzaldehyde (CHO).

This is the Etard reaction where Acetophenone is reduced with Zn-Hg, HCl.

(R) → (5)

This is the Gattermann-Koch reaction.

(S) → (2)

Phenol undergoes reduction with Zn, Δ to give Benzene, which then undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with CO + HCl in presence of AlCl₃ to give Benzaldehyde (CHO).

This is the Rosenmund reduction where the product Benzaldehyde is obtained from the Friedel-Crafts carbonylation of benzene.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The number of oxygen atoms present in the major product (having two cyclic rings) of the following reaction is
B.sol_text:
Answer: 03.00

Solution:

The starting material is 3-methoxyphenol (or resorcinol monomethyl ether) with a benzene ring bearing -OCH₃ and -OH groups.

Step 1: The aromatic compound reacts with the Meldrum's acid derivative (shown as a reagent with formyl and carboxylic acid chloride groups).

Step 2: Friedel-Crafts type acylation occurs, with the acyl group attaching to the benzene ring, forming an intermediate with:
- The benzene ring
- -OCH₃ group
- -O-C(=O)-CH₂-C(=O)Cl group (acylated at the hydroxyl position)

Step 3: Under H₂SO₄ and heat, intramolecular cyclization occurs through Friedel-Crafts acylation, where the carbonyl carbon forms a bond with the benzene ring, creating the first cyclic ring (a coumarin-like structure).

Step 4: The second cyclization follows, where another intramolecular reaction creates a second six-membered ring fused to the first, forming a chromanone structure.

The final major product has two cyclic rings with the structure shown:
- A benzene ring fused to a pyranone (chroman-4-one type) ring system
- An additional oxygen in a second lactone/pyranone ring

Counting oxygen atoms in the major product with two cyclic rings:
- One oxygen in the methoxy group (-OCH₃): 1 oxygen
- One oxygen in the first lactone carbonyl (C=O): 1 oxygen
- One oxygen in the second lactone carbonyl (C=O): 1 oxygen

Total number of oxygen atoms = 3
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: In a bag there are three tickets numbered 1, 2, 3. A ticket is drawn at random and put back and this is done four times. The probability that the sum of the numbers is even, is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (1)
Solution:
The total number of ways of selecting 4 tickets
= 3^4 = 81
The favourable number of ways
= sum of coefficients of x^2, x^4, ....... in (x + x^2 + x^3)^4

= sum of coefficients of x^2, x^4, ...... in x^4(1 + x + x^2)^4.

Let (1 + x + x^2)^4 = 1 + a₁x + a₂x^2 + ..... + a₈x^8.
Then 3^4 = 1 + a₁ + a₂ + a₃ + .... + a₈, (On putting x = 1)
and 1 = 1 - a₁ + a₂ - a₃ + ..... + a₈ , (On putting x = -1)
∴ 3^4 + 1 = 2(1 + a₂ + a₄ + a₆ + a₈)
⇒ a₂ + a₄ + a₆ + a₈ = 41
Thus sum of the coefficients of x^2, x^4, ...... = 41
Hence the required probability = 41/81.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The position vectors of the vertices of a quadrilateral ABCD are a⃗, b⃗, c⃗ and d⃗ respectively. Area of the quadrilateral formed by joining the middle points of its sides is
A.sol_text:
It is given that a⃗, b⃗, c⃗ and d⃗ are the position vectors of vertices of a quadrilateral ABCD respectively.
Let E, F, G and H are the middle points of sides AB, BC, CD and DA respectively.
The position vectors of these points will be
OE⃗ = (1/2)(a⃗ + b⃗), OF⃗ = (1/2)(b⃗ + c⃗),
OG⃗ = (1/2)(c⃗ + d⃗), OH⃗ = (1/2)(a⃗ + d⃗)

Then EF⃗ = OF⃗ - OE⃗ = ((c⃗ - a⃗)/2)

and FG⃗ = (1/2)(d⃗ - b⃗), GH⃗ = (1/2)(a⃗ - c⃗), GH⃗ = (1/2)(b⃗ - d⃗)

It is clear that EF⃗ is parallel to GH⃗ and FG⃗ is parallel to HE⃗. Thus EFGH is a parallelogram.

∴ EF⃗ × FG⃗ = (1/4){(c⃗ - a⃗) × (d⃗ - b⃗)}

= (1/4)(c⃗ × d⃗ - c⃗ × b⃗ - a⃗ × d⃗ + a⃗ × b⃗)

= (1/4)(a⃗ × b⃗ + b⃗ × c⃗ + c⃗ × d⃗ + d⃗ × a⃗)

∴ Area of parallelogram EFGH is,
A = |EF⃗ × FG⃗| = (1/4)|a⃗ × b⃗ + b⃗ × c⃗ + c⃗ × d⃗ + d⃗ × a⃗|.

A.text: There are three identical boxes I, II, III, each containing two coins. In box I, both coins are gold coins, in box II both are silver coins and in the box III, there is one gold and one silver coin. A person chooses a box at random and takes out a coin. If the coin is of gold, then the probability that the other coin in the box is also of gold, is
A.sol_text:
Let E₁, E₂, E₃ be the events respectively that boxes I, II and III are chosen.
∴P(E₁) = P(E₂) = P(E₃) = 1/3
Let A be the event that 'the coin drawn is of gold'
∴ P(A/E₁) = P(a gold coin from bag I) = 2/2 = 1

P(A/E₂) = P(a gold coin from bag II) = 0
P(A/E₃) = P(a gold coin from bag III) = 1/2
∴Required probability =
P(E₁/A) = [P(E₁)·P(A/E₁)] / [P(E₁)·P(A/E₁) + P(E₂)·P(A/E₂) + P(E₃)·P(A/E₃)]
= [(1/3)×1] / [(1/3)×1 + (1/3)×0 + (1/3)×(1/2)]
= (1/3) / [(1/3) + 0 + 1/6]
= (1/3) / [(2+1)/6]
= (1/3) / (1/2)
= 2/3

A.text:
A vector vec(a) = xi + yj + zk makes an obtuse angle with y-axis, makes equal angles with vectors vec(b) and vec(c) and vec(a) is perpendicular to vec(d) ≡ i - j + 2k. If |vec(a)| = 2√3, then vector vec(a) is

vec(b) = yi - 2zj + 3xk
vec(c) = 2zi + 3xj - yk
A.sol_text:
Given vec(a) ≡ (x, y, z) = xi + yj + zk makes an obtuse angle with y-axis
∴ vec(a)·j < 0 ⇒ y < 0

Also, given vec(a) makes equal angles with vectors vec(b) and vec(c)
∴ (vec(a)·vec(b))/(|vec(a)||vec(b)|) = (vec(a)·vec(c))/(|vec(a)||vec(c)|)

⇒ (vec(a)·vec(b))/|vec(b)| = (vec(a)·vec(c))/|vec(c)|

⇒ (xy - 2yz + 3xz)/(√(y^2 + 4z^2 + 9x^2)) = (2xz + 3xy - yz)/(√(4z^2 + 9x^2 + y^2))

⇒ 2xy + yz - zx = 0     ...(i)

Also, given vec(a)·vec(d) = 0
⇒ x - y + 2z = 0
⇒ x = (y - x)/2     ...(ii)
∴ From (i) and (ii)
2xy + (y - x)·(y - x)/2 = 0
⇒ (y + x)^2 = 0 ⇒ y = -x and so from (ii),
z = (-x - x)/2 = -x

∴ vec(a) ≡ (x, -x, -x)

But given |vec(a)| = 2√3
⇒ √(x^2 + x^2 + x^2) = 2√3
⇒ √(3x^2) = 2√3 ⇒ x = 2

∴ vec(a) ≡ (2, -2, -2)
